correctness.rationale: Let P be the affine pushforward from shift-invariant trajectory measures to their time-zero marginals. For an extreme marginal mu, the fiber P^{-1}(mu) is a nonempty compact convex face: any convex decomposition of a point in the fiber pushes forward to a convex decomposition of mu, so both endpoints remain in the fiber. An extreme point of that face is extreme among all shift-invariant measures and hence ergodic, proving existence of an ergodic lift. Birkhoff applied to f composed with evaluation and disintegration over evaluation then give the almost-everywhere existence of a trajectory realizing the marginal mean. The two-direction circle example has exactly two ergodic component measures with the same Haar marginal, so their half-half mixture is a nonergodic chosen lift of an extreme marginal. The complete Suda preprint was read; its Theorem 3.7 makes the invalid stronger chosen-lift inference, confirming that the audited distinction is mathematically necessary.

originality.rationale: The positive existence mechanism is standard compact-convex geometry and ordinary factor-map theory already records existence of ergodic lifts of ergodic factor measures. However, the audited scientific claim is a correction of the current Suda trajectory-space theorem: the complete primary text explicitly states Theorem 3.7 as 'Extremal invariant measures are finely ergodic' for a displayed lift and its proof incorrectly infers extremality of that lift from extremality of its pushforward. The explicit two-direction circle system refutes the stronger chosen-lift reading, while the face argument gives the sharp existential replacement and recovers a concrete almost-everywhere time-average value in Suda's nonunique-trajectory setting. No checked source states this exact failure/repair package in that framework.

value.rationale: The distinction fixes a central logical bridge between base-space extremality and trajectory-space Birkhoff theory in a current nonunique-orbit framework. It prevents an incorrect arbitrary-lift conclusion, identifies the strongest valid replacement, and preserves a concrete almost-everywhere time-average consequence. A sharp correction with an explicit counterexample and surviving theorem is substantively motivated.

limitations: The theorem applies to extreme points of the affine image of shift-invariant trajectory measures.
It does not prove that every measure ergodic in Suda's strong-backward-invariance sense is extreme.
The counterexample does not assume the switching axiom, which is also absent from the corrected extremal-lift statement.
